snapshot: human-authorized RPA recovery and root-step handoff controls

starting_state.reason: No new source-level cue separates the paused scanner remainder from known controls; the pass resumed the four saved emitted-record cursors.

saved_cursor_results.result: The external row is PRA runtime schema source.

rotated_queries.result: Known Project-AI-Ceta control already classified as BV-102; not reopened.

aggregate.method: GitHub default-branch code search. Search rows were treated only as locators; selected original files, complete pinned trees, commit history and public issue history were read before classification.

selected_repositories.selected_reason: Only saved-cursor external hit; its complete tree contains sanitized real-machine request/result/receipt evidence.
Lower-arity parent/child query exposes committed run-shaped handoff records with a direct project statement distinguishing graph-step recovery from live sub-agent execution.

project_context.finding: The root instructions and owner boundary describe an internal family-farm automation system. The current controller is a human manager; an AI sales agent is future scope and must use the same validation and authorization interfaces.

event_sequence.event: A human-confirmed write request is created for one item in commit mode.
The worker begins the write attempt.
The worker returns UNKNOWN after the controlled post-confirmation readback interruption; reconciliation is pending and manual review is initially required.
The importer accepts the result receipt.
The importer creates a single read-only reconciliation request bound to the source result.
Read-only reconciliation returns VERIFIED, clears reconciliation pending and closes manual review without another write click.
The importer accepts the reconciliation receipt.
The committed validator records all binding, count, database-ledger, review-closure, single-reconcile and write-lock checks true.

implementation_context.finding: Source imports an immutable result, and only when an item reports a needs-reconciliation state does it ensure one follow-up reconciliation attempt. The acceptance report says that follow-up is read-only and deliberately fault-injected.

dependency_assessment.provider_or_model_attribution: None. ShadowBot here is a bounded RPA worker; the canonical project documents the current controller as human and AI sales control as future scope.

public_issue.finding: The issue publicly describes the producer-to-renderer boundary, real local-model reproduction, planned root/child recovery checks and maintainer authorization. It is prior reporting, not an original discovery.

pupu_control.finding: The selected snapshot contains two content-addressed handoff events with parent/child run fields and full-output envelopes. However, the project's verification report explicitly states that the shipped default graph had no sub-agent node or toolkit, so a delegated live question was unreachable; generic kernel sub-agent records were regression tests. The accompanying real-model probe contains one local model run, no parent/child run and no agent identity. These are root graph-step and human-input recovery records, not two autonomous AI participants.
pupu_control.prior_reporting: The public issue predates and describes the controlled verification. Even absent that report, the original records fail the independent-participant gate.

alternatives.designed_automation: Decisive for both families. PRA deliberately creates one read-only recovery after an UNKNOWN result; PuPu deliberately tests human-input resume and renderer recovery.
alternatives.single_operator_or_owner: Both projects retain explicit human or maintainer control. Public process/run labels do not establish independently operated agents.
alternatives.repeated_tests: PuPu's kernel sub-agent matches are explicitly regression evidence. PRA's selected package is a real-machine controlled fault test, not uncontrolled behavior.
alternatives.shared_state_fault: PuPu investigates recovery-state defects inside one product. PRA validates the intended recovery path rather than a cross-operator coordination event.
alternatives.observer_contamination: Eighteen self-index rows were separated. The Project-AI-Ceta row is a registered BV-102 control and was not reopened.

github_code_queries: "No subagent node or subagent toolkit is configured"
"generic kernel subagent tests are regression evidence"
prior_reporting_check.result: No prior coordination report was located for the PRA process chain in the exact checked scope as of 2026-10-25; exact phrases resolve only to the origin repository. PuPu issue 224 is itself a prior public report and implementation brief. Search absence does not establish global novelty, and neither family qualifies as autonomous cross-operator AI coordination.

classification.result: human-authorized RPA recovery and root-step handoff controls
classification.reason: PRA preserves a real content-specific process handoff with downstream use, but neither process is established as an AI agent and the human-controlled system intentionally creates the recovery. PuPu preserves content-addressed parent/child handoff records, but the project explicitly says no live sub-agent was configured in those runs and the episode was already publicly reported.

missing_evidence_to_advance: For PRA: primary evidence that both sender and recipient were autonomous AI participants rather than a bounded RPA worker and importer/recovery process.
For either family: independent runtime and operator provenance for distinguishable AI participants.
A recipient action outside the documented recovery/test topology and human or maintainer authorization.
Primary owner, operator or policy evidence that the cooperation itself crossed an authorization boundary.

next_cursors.rationale: Requires two run identities plus content-addressed use.
Adds attributable agent and event-time fields missing from the PuPu control.
Looks for separately hashed source and recipient results.
Looks for provider-attributed message transfer and causal use.

safeguards.sanitization: Original public report, index, issue and commit links plus event/observation timestamps and Git hashes are retained. Product identities, raw run/task/session identifiers, payload bodies, local paths, addresses, credentials, tokens and private logs are omitted.
